paper.title_en: Adaptive proposals for nonparametric equation-of-state inference with RIFT: iterative Gaussian-process refinement in a compressed sequence representation
paper.abstract_en: Nonparametric equation-of-state (EOS) models have two practical problems for Bayesian inference: too many parameters, introducing observationally inaccessible degrees of freedom; and no painless route to adaptive refinement, necessary to forecast future observing scenarios. In this work we address both problems, providing a framework for adaptive nonparametric EOS sampling which simultaneously provides insight into the observationally-accessible effective dimensions. Applied to a published Gaussian-process ensemble, this analysis reveals substantial sound-speed freedom beyond what observations demand. Conversely, by concrete example, we demonstrate that often-used schemes to use many EOS realizations will invariably break down when challenged by new physics, as the observationally-accessible dimension increases substantially. These functional adaptive sampling tools provide a path forward to efficient computation, interpretation, and discovery for future analyses of cold, beta-equilibrium nuclear matter.
